analysis.note: Past passive participial stem from √han, agreeing with the implied second-person subject; Śaṅkara glosses it as hataḥ san.
Indeclinable disjunctive particle, paired with the later vā.
Future 2nd singular of pra-√āp, ‘you will attain.’
Object of prāpsyasi; glossed by Śaṅkara as svargaṃ prāpsyasi.
Second member of the vā ... vā alternation.
Future 2nd singular middle ending with active/kartari sense; Śaṅkara construes mahīm as its object.
Ablative-form indeclinable used inferentially, ‘therefore’; sandhi before uttiṣṭha gives tasmād.
Imperative 2nd singular of ud-√sthā, ‘stand up, arise.’

Bahuvrīhi compound used predicatively of the addressed warrior. I remove the editorial hyphen from the morphological stem/surface for verification: the printed form is kṛta-niścayaḥ, but the inflected compound stem is kṛtaniścaya. The verifier logged bahuvrīhi relation as unsupported rather than deriving an alternative; I retain the bahuvrīhi analysis because the commentary’s niścayaṃ kṛtvā supports ‘one by whom a resolve has been made.’ The commentary line appears noisy at ‘kṛtāni ca yaḥ,’ but the following niścayaṃ kṛtvā clearly glosses kṛta-niścayaḥ.

verification.detail: compound stem kṛtaniścaya as Pum/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara explicitly glosses hato as hataḥ san, ‘being slain,’ and repeats svargaṃ prāpsyasi. His later paraphrase of the resolve includes mariṣyāmi vā, ‘or I shall die,’ confirming the death-alternative rather than an active sense such as ‘having killed.’
options_considered: hataḥ as passive ‘slain/being killed’ agreeing with the implied tvam
hataḥ merely as ‘struck’ without implication of death
justifications.chosen: hataḥ means ‘slain,’ predicated of the addressed warrior; svargam is the heaven attained after that death.

evidence.quote: hato vā prāpsyasi svargam, hataḥ san svargaṃ prāpsyasi |
evidence.translation: ‘Slain, you will attain heaven’—being slain, you will attain heaven.

evidence.quote: jeṣyāmi śatrūn, mariṣyāmi vā iti niścayaṃ kṛtvety arthaḥ
evidence.translation: The meaning is: having made the resolve, ‘I shall conquer the enemies, or I shall die.’

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara supplies the object of jitvā as karṇādīn śūrān, ‘brave men such as Karṇa,’ and keeps mahīm as the object of bhokṣyase. Thus the sequence is defeat the enemy heroes, then enjoy the earth—not simply ‘conquer the earth.’
options_considered: ‘having conquered the earth, you will enjoy it’
‘having conquered Karṇa and other warriors, you will enjoy the earth’
justifications.chosen: jitvā refers to conquering enemy warriors, while bhokṣyase mahīm means enjoying or possessing the earth after victory.

evidence.quote: jitvā vā karṇādīn śūrān bhokṣyase mahīm |
evidence.translation: Or, having conquered brave men such as Karṇa, you will enjoy the earth.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara states the intended force directly: in both ways there is only gain for you. This controls the rhetoric of the verse as consolation/encouragement, not as a neutral prediction of two possibilities.
options_considered: a neutral ‘or ... or’ with no stated evaluative force
a two-branch argument that both outcomes are gain
justifications.chosen: The paired vā ... vā presents two alternatives, both advantageous to Arjuna.

evidence.translation: The intention is: in either case, there is only gain for you.

justifications.decision: The commentary gives the correlative reasoning yata evaṃ tasmāt, ‘since this is so, therefore,’ so tasmāt is not a spatial/source ablative in the translation but the conclusion drawn from the preceding alternatives.
justifications.chosen: tasmāt is inferential ‘therefore,’ introducing the command uttiṣṭha, ‘arise.’

evidence.quote: yata evaṃ tasmāt uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya
evidence.translation: Since this is so, therefore stand up, O Kaunteya, for battle.

justifications.decision: The commentary’s line is textually noisy at ‘kṛtāni ca yaḥ,’ which I take as a corruption around kṛta-niścayaḥ; the immediately following niścayaṃ kṛtvā, ‘having made the resolve,’ fixes the sense. Śaṅkara also supplies the content of that resolve: ‘I shall conquer the enemies, or I shall die.’ For morphology I record the unhyphenated compound stem kṛtaniścaya; the hyphen is only the printed representation in the source.
options_considered: karmadhāraya-like ‘fixed/settled resolve’ as an abstract description
bahuvrīhi/actional ‘one by whom a resolve has been made,’ with the resolve’s content supplied
justifications.chosen: kṛta-niścayaḥ is a bahuvrīhi: ‘one whose resolve has been made,’ rendered ‘with your resolve made / having made your resolve.’

evidence.quote: yata evaṃ tasmāt uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtāni ca yaḥ jeṣyāmi śatrūn, mariṣyāmi vā iti niścayaṃ kṛtvety arthaḥ ||bhgs_2.37||
evidence.translation: Since this is so, therefore stand up, O Kaunteya, for battle—the meaning is: having made the resolve, ‘I shall conquer the enemies, or I shall die.’

justifications.decision: The commentary merely repeats kaunteya, so the choice rests on grammar and lexicon: the -a stem vocative singular is kaunteya, and MW identifies kaunteya as a metronymic from Kuntī, a name of Arjuna.
options_considered: nominative proper noun or unrelated lexical item
justifications.chosen: kaunteya is a vocative metronym, ‘O son of Kuntī.’

translation:
If slain, you will attain heaven (svarga);
or, having conquered, you will enjoy the earth.
Therefore arise, O son of Kuntī (Kaunteya),
for battle, with your resolve (niścaya) made.
one_shot_delta: Without Śaṅkara, one might take hataḥ weakly as ‘struck’ or even construe it actively; the bhāṣya’s hataḥ san and mariṣyāmi vā make it the ‘slain/die’ alternative.
A commentary-blind rendering might say simply ‘having conquered, enjoy the earth’; Śaṅkara specifies that what is conquered is Karṇa and other warriors, while the earth is enjoyed afterward.
The verse’s logic could be missed as mere either/or prediction; Śaṅkara states that both alternatives are gain for Arjuna.
kṛta-niścayaḥ might be flattened to ‘determined’; Śaṅkara gives the concrete resolve: ‘I shall conquer the enemies, or I shall die.’
analyzer_disagreements: hataḥ: ByT5 lemmatizes the form as han; for a nominal participial form I give the subanta stem hata as lemma, while noting derivation from √han.
prāpsyasi: ByT5 gives prāp as the lemma; I split the form according to the requested format into prefix pra plus bare root āp.
uttiṣṭha: ByT5 gives the lexicalized lemma utthā; I analyze it as prefix ud plus bare root sthā, with Lot Madhyama singular.

kṛta-niścayaḥ: ByT5 splits kṛta and niścayaḥ as separate items; the printed compound and Śaṅkara’s gloss niścayaṃ kṛtvā justify treating it as one compound stem kṛtaniścaya, with the printed hyphen excluded from the morphological lemma/surface.
open_questions: Line 4 appears unproofread or corrupt at ‘kṛtāni ca yaḥ’; I have not emended the quotation, but interpret it through the clear gloss ‘niścayaṃ kṛtvā.’

The verifier reported the bahuvrīhi relation for kṛtaniścayaḥ as unsupported, not as disproved; I therefore retain the commentary-based bahuvrīhi analysis while normalizing the compound stem without the printed hyphen.
mula: hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm | tasmād uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛta-niścayaḥ
